title: Incremental output protocol: SDK compatibility patterns and cross-language examples
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Define and ship a compatibility layer and reference examples across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs that support incremental (streamed) model outputs, first-class tool/function calling, and typed/structured outputs. The goal is to provide idiomatic language bindings that surface the same runtime semantics: event envelope, backpressure, resumability, and deterministic structured emission for evals and downstream processing.

Scope:
- Wire protocol: finalize a compact event envelope (delta, tool_call, tool_result, structured_chunk, done, error) and documented ordering guarantees.
- Client-side patterns: short reference APIs that make it ergonomic to consume progressive structured outputs and to call tools as first-class async functions.
- Graceful migration: compatibility shims for older SDK users that consume token streams (char deltas) instead of structured chunks.
- Tests/examples: three in-repo examples (TS web worker consumer, Python async iterator pipeline, Go channel-based consumer) + end-to-end PRs.

Non-goals: full runtime implementation for Dedicated; we focus on SDK surface and examples that drive runtime changes already tracked in runtime-1.19 workstream.
acceptance_criteria: Wire format documented in a single markdown spec and linked from SDK repos
TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs expose an idiomatic IncrementalInvocation API that returns a unified event stream type
Reference examples compile and run in CI with integration smoke tests against staging API
Backward-compatible shim for 'token delta' consumers included and covered by unit tests
Performance: streaming helper introduces <5% median latency increase for normal requests in canary
notes: Decision: use an event-envelope JSON lines (ndjson) over the streaming transport to simplify intermediaries and proxies. Each line is a single canonical event with 'type' and opaque 'id' for correlation.
Tradeoff: binary framing (gRPC) would be more efficient, but ndjson maximizes compatibility with browsers and existing fetch/stream patterns.
Compatibility: shims will emit legacy 'delta' events by concatenating structured chunk values until the consumer requests legacy mode.

Backpressure: Node/TS consumer will expose an async iterator with manual pull (next()) and a highWaterMark option for buffering. Python will mirror with an 'aiter()' async generator controlling read-ahead. Go exposes a channel with a configurable buffer size and Close/Retries semantics.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Maya Chen: Drafted protocol spec (see design doc link). Early feedback requested from SDK owners in TS/Py/Go.
2026-03-01 - Diego Ruiz: Reviewed TS API sketch; suggested explicit 'onToolCall' hook rather than implicit side-channel to keep synchronous tool registration ergonomic.
2026-03-03 - Priya Nair: Security review: ensure tool invocation IDs are namespaced per-tenant to avoid cross-tenant leak in logs. Flagged for runtime instrumentation.

2026-03-05 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented TS prototype in branch 'feat/incremental-protocol-ts' and pushed PR #2047. Self-test shows structured JSON events arrive before 'done' event even when tool calls are pending.

2026-03-08 - QA: Ran integration against staging; observed rare ordering inversion when client reconnects during active tool call — root cause likely on runtime retry policy. Added as dependency to runtime ticket ENG-852900.
2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor: Updated examples and added Python async iterator sample. Marking core API surface stable; will iterate on error semantics in follow-up.
samples: Compatibility shim note: the TS shim includes client.asLegacyTokenStream() that emits 'delta' events by flattening structured_chunk payloads; the shim is gated behind an option to avoid accidental usage.
qa_plan: Unit tests: cover envelope parsing and error paths in each SDK
Integration: end-to-end examples run against staging API in CI with tool-call simulation
Performance: run latency comparison between streaming and non-streaming calls; validate <5% regression threshold
Chaos: test reconnects and resumability with simulated network interruptions
risks: Runtime ordering semantics during retries may produce surprising tool call interleavings; mitigation: sequence ids and idempotency tokens in envelope
NDJSON increases bandwidth slightly; may affect high-volume embedding micro-batch flows — monitor in canary
